messages:
Renata: Observed incident: hosted master key rotation -> private adapters hit 401 for ~25s. Question: which layer owns orchestration for credential rebinds (control plane push vs adapter pull)?

Michael: TL;DR: control plane should be authoritative but adapters must support resilient pull when control plane unreachable. Hybrid mode seems right.

Ashley: Agreed for hybrid. Private/air-gapped installs can't depend on push. Need a signed-lease that adapters can validate offline.

Tom: Proposed signed-lease shape: base64-signed blob with adapter_id, tenant_id, exp, nonce. Adapter verifies sig and swaps local creds. No control-plane call required to validate.

Renata: Failure log snippet:
```
ERROR auth: token expired
adapter=sidecar-private req=xyz-1
```
Adapters retried aggressively and hit hosted rate limits.

SRE-Leah: Ops constraints: no thundering herds to control plane during rotations. Require adapter backoff + server-side tenant degradation heuristics (metric: auth.rebind_failures).

Michael: Two candidate flows for RFC: (1) Push-first: control-plane pushes rotation events over long-lived channel; adapters accept atomically, fallback to signed-lease. (2) Pull-first: adapter pulls from local KMS or uses signed-lease, control plane is auditor.

Tom: Also note: KV cache invalidation during rebinds. We should ensure request-scoped auth tokens or a barrier that flushes per-request KV entries during swap.

Ashley: Config sketch (adapter):
```
adapter.auth_mode: hybrid
adapter.signed_lease_ttl_s: 300
adapter.max_rebinds_per_min: 5
adapter.kms_local: http://127.0.0.1:8200
```
Default to hybrid and 300s TTL to balance security and reliability.

SRE-Leah: Add metrics & runbook: auth.rebind_attempts, auth.rebind_failures, auth.rebind_backoff_seconds. If failures >5 in 60s => mark tenant degraded and route to fallback model.

Renata: Actions: Michael+Tom write RFC comparing push vs pull (include signed-lease format, KV-barrier), Ashley opens config PR, Leah drafts runbook & metrics dashboard. I'll attach repro logs.
